findings.evidence: 16 queries (8 should-trigger, 8 should-not); optimizing-descriptions asks for about 20, with 8-10 on each side and near-misses.
findings.fix: Add four realistic queries, two should-trigger and two near-miss should-not-trigger (for example a session-wake or reviewer-setup prompt that shares runner words but belongs to the neighbour skills), keeping the existing near-misses.

findings.evidence: Six cases with verifiable assertions and two input files, but no case for the hard-tier wait (exit 75 with retry_after_s=) or the GSD retry/skip/abort answer, which sections 6 and 7 make the fragile path.
findings.fix: Add one eval whose prompt includes an AIKIT-XAI line with exit=75 and retry_after_s=, and assertions that the caller waits once for that many seconds, re-invokes the same runtime and model, and answers abort for every other non-zero exit.

findings.evidence: ## When to use restates the description: "When a run, a review or an execution step calls an external AI CLI and acts on the result."
findings.fix: Delete the section and record the removal; the description already carries WHEN, and the body is invisible until the skill has triggered.

findings.evidence: ## Pitfalls lists specific facts but several have no why: "Atomic rewrites keep the file mode. Replacing a config or state file by hand can drop it."
findings.fix: Add the consequence to each pitfall that lacks one, for example that a hand replacement drops the 0600 mode the runner set, so a later read of the state file is refused.

findings.evidence: Description has WHAT, WHEN, keywords and a boundary, but it is third-person capability prose ("Covers the hard-tier wait") rather than the imperative "Use this skill when" form.
findings.fix: Use when you run, wait for, read, retry or chain an external AI CLI (pi, opencode, codex, cursor, copilot, claude) through ai-kit's cross-AI runner (cross-ai.mjs): pick one runtime and model, pass the call's settings (role, effort, context, session id, skills, MCP servers), launch the runner, read its exit code, its per-setting report and its last AIKIT-XAI stderr line, resume a session in a second round, and answer a stop. Use this skill when a lane hits quota, a rate limit or a 429, exits 75 or 69, prints retry_after_s=, reports a setting ignored, or needs an --argv-file for a CLI the runner has no formula for. It covers the hard-tier wait, the user notice, GSD's retry/skip/abort answer and the rule to never switch harness, provider or model. Not for reviewer setup or GSD config (those are ai-kit-spec-config and ai-kit-gsd-curated-config).

findings.evidence: The launch reference is gated ("MANDATORY before the first launch on a host"), but five host sections repeat the same unverified foreground-wait instruction.
findings.fix: Keep the Claude Code pattern and one foreground-wait section, and name pi, opencode, cursor, codex and copilot as hosts that use it; do not load a separate file for a single host.

findings.evidence: The hard-tier wake offers two equal paths: CronCreate when callable, otherwise print-and-stop, with no default for a host that is not Claude Code.
findings.fix: Default every host but Claude Code to print retry_after_s, the state path and the re-invoke command and stop; mention CronCreate only as the Claude Code escape hatch.

findings.evidence: capS is given as 14400 with no source URL or date checked, and the skill does not tell the caller to read it live; the runner template does currently set capS to 14400.
findings.fix: Point the reader at the runner's CONFIG capS (skills/ai-kit-spec-review/references/cross-ai.mjs) as the live read, or cite the vendor-or-repo source and the date checked next to 14400.

findings.evidence: The outer deadline is min(CONFIG outerTimeoutS, GSD's workflow.cross_ai_timeout or gsd-core's 300 s default), but the skill never says where CONFIG or that GSD key is read from.
findings.fix: Name the file and key the runner reads for outerTimeoutS and workflow.cross_ai_timeout, the same way section 6 names the state-file path.
